displayedInputs.question: Of 40 people, 10 meet the standard. What percentage meet the standard? First calculate \(10 \div 40 \times 100\). Calculate: \(10 \div 40 \times 100 = ?\)
Calculate: \(20 \div 0.4 = ?\) (Give your answer as a decimal.)
Calculate: \(30 \div 0.5 = ?\) (Give your answer as a decimal.)
\(25\%\) of a book has been read, which is exactly 40 pages. How many pages are in the whole book? Calculate: \(40 \div 0.25 = ?\) (Give your answer as a decimal.)
What are pie charts suitable for showing?

choices.A: How much of the total each part represents
choices.B: How a quantity changes over time
choices.C: Only what the largest number is

displayedInputs.question: There are 50 students in a class, and \(40\%\) like soccer. How many students like soccer? Calculate: \(50 \times 40 \div 100 = ?\)
Square dot arrays: 1, 4, 9. The number after 9 is \(9 + 7\). What is \(9 + 7\)? Calculate: \(9 + 7 = ?\)

choices.A: Quantities with meanings opposite to those represented by positive numbers
choices.C: They can only represent temperature and cannot represent anything else
